title: Pastry, Chinese, made with rice flour

content.title: About
content.content: Chinese rice‑flour pastry is a traditional dessert made from a thin dough of rice flour, often filled with sweet red bean, sesame paste, or fruit. The dough is soft and slightly sticky, giving the finished pastry a delicate rice aroma and gentle sweetness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice‑flour dough makes the pastry gluten‑free, important for people with celiac disease.
In China these pastries are commonly served during tea ceremonies as a light sweet between dishes.
Traditionally they are steamed, but modern versions can be baked for a crispier crust.
Fillings range from sweet red bean to fragrant lotus seed paste.
Baking with rice flour creates a slightly crunchy outer layer.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Rice flour contains no gluten, making the pastry safe for those with gluten intolerance.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with wheat‑based baked goods, these pastries usually contain less saturated fat.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Rice flour provides slow‑releasing carbohydrates that help maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice flour supplies thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: The pastry offers magnesium and phosphorus, beneficial for muscle and bone health.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may be allergic to rice flour.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rice flour can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium in fillings
items.content: Certain fillings (e.g., soy‑based sauces) may add extra sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The pastry can be enjoyed on its own, served with tea, or used as a base for fruit salads. Cut into bite‑size pieces and pair with berries or a drizzle of honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the pastries in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C; reheat by steaming or microwaving before serving.
